title: Aerrow
dek: A scout who seeks freedom through strength, learns the cost of overreaching in Babel’s wilds and helps turn dangerous journeys into supplies for the Refuge.

facts.February hunt: Two deaths; Arjahn’s first Revivify is followed by a second death and later restoration by Elenia
facts.Babel role: Scout, supply hunter and advocate of route preparation
facts.Core tension: Craves battle; admits fear and depends on others’ skills
facts.Later record: Warns of slain natives and directs the company toward the caverns; subsequent whereabouts unresolved

body:
Aerrow is a Shadar-kai sorcerer and scout whose work in Babel-Ashur joins reconnaissance, gathering and dangerous hunts. He seeks physical perfection and resists the servitude he associates with his people, yet learns to rely on companions whose skills differ from his own.

Recognizing another warrior

Aerrow and Aravil meet while practicing at the range. He calls her an ally and speaks of feeling slow after his arrival; she says she is finally finding her stride. They recognize a shared longing for the front. The exchange records their affinity without making either character’s judgments universal.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4.

What he wants from the front

At the range, Aerrow is practicing with Booming Blade when Aravil greets him. He speaks of a shared struggle among people of the shadow and welcomes her as an ally. He feels slow after arriving and finds the settlement soft beside the violence he misses. The appetite is for the heightened feeling of fighting for his life; he calls the pursuit of power tiring.

That longing does not make him indiscriminately trusting of dangerous people. He warns Aravil about Fredrick, who appears harmless yet nearly overcame him in the arena. Aravil sees potential usefulness where Aerrow sees a threat. Their kinship permits agreement about belonging at the front and disagreement about whom to accept beside them.

January · gathering is dangerous work

Aerrow joins Aravil and Arjahn in searching beyond the Refuge for the resources a lasting camp needs. He admits how poorly he reads the unfamiliar jungle, follows Aravil’s quieter path and proposes equipment that might help future journeys. The first outing yields buried carvings and components from defeated creatures; it does not yield an explanation of the lost civilization.

The larger company then fights an aqualisk and demodragons. Aerrow is badly hurt before Eugene finishes the aqualisk. Healing restores his body faster than he can make sense of the experience. His appetite for glory coexists with caution: he urges the hunters to gather quickly, leave the carcasses and return with materials for the builders. A later hunt with Eugene and Aravil includes an escape from an unidentified threat and a hard-won serpent kill whose harvest fails.

Glory, noise and another person’s skill

On the first supply journey Aerrow asks Aravil about both hunting and avoiding the island’s predators. He proposes covered high ground and warns that spoken holy magic can betray a hiding place. Arjahn answers his wish for a glorious death with a different hope: dying meaningfully. Aerrow accepts the distinction and the possibility that an emergency may force the cleric to make noise.

His own field senses do not immediately match his confidence. He finds no signs in the unfamiliar land and struggles to stay quiet, then follows Aravil’s tracks and tells her she should lead. He begins carefully excavating buried carvings when the group finds them. The warrior eager for danger can also learn, defer and gather something useful without a fight.

The body heals before the memory

After the aqualisk nearly breaks him, Aerrow briefly wishes he had stayed with Pristinia’s feather beds. Arjahn has already healed the injuries and asks what is still wrong. Aerrow’s answer is that his body feels fine; his memory has not caught up. The desire for a life-or-death struggle has met an experience he cannot immediately absorb.

Arjahn responds with practical sympathy about the nightmares such encounters can leave. Aerrow still thinks about which materials to gather, but wants the company moving before other creatures come to feed. Healing enables the return journey. It does not require him to feel invulnerable or eager for another encounter.

February · a return that does not last

With Aravil missing, Aerrow goes out with Arjahn to find supplies for a safer shelter. He tries to keep his angry companion focused on the job rather than revenge. Arjahn agrees not to pursue danger at the cost of Aerrow’s life, but an aqualisk and its accompanying demodragons overwhelm the pair.

The combat record shows Aerrow dying, Arjahn casting Revivify and Aerrow returning with a single point of life. Renewed attacks kill him again. Arjahn escapes with his body, bringing him back to the cave through repeated magical jumps. This temporary Revivify must remain distinct from the later restoration after the retreat.

A companion brought home, and a warning heard

The main Babel quest later finds Arjahn beside Aerrow’s preserved body. Arjahn says he withheld his only powerful diamond and judges that choice harshly. Elenia calls for aid and the scene explicitly describes her raising the scout. The checked passage does not name her spell. Arjahn’s self-blame records his moral crisis rather than proving that he caused every danger the hunters faced.

Aerrow’s later warning at the Refuge therefore comes from someone who has already suffered the wilderness’s cost. His report of slain natives and approaching monsters deserves attention without making his suspicions about every enemy plan certain. Follow the hunts, their losses and the work they support →

A rescue begins with learning the ground

When Wren returns from petrification, she wants to go after Aravil immediately. She credits Aerrow with making her recognize that the company first needs to learn how to navigate the island. They begin comparing remembered routes and building a map. His contribution reaches beyond whatever he can kill or harvest.

The advice belongs beside his own experience of being brought home dead from the failed hunt and later raised by Elenia. He has reason to take preparation seriously. The record does not make him the sole author of the map or the later rescue; it shows him helping redirect urgency into work that other companions can use.

The warning that leads toward the captives

Aerrow’s later scouting report brings the threatened civilians into the company’s planning. He says he found dozens of natives torn apart while searching for food and fears that the hunters are closing on the caves. Asked where, he points to the familiar Caverns Below.

When the others debate what the giants are doing, he admits the limits of their knowledge: they only know that Elenia had trouble reaching the sky island and speculate that the hunters may want what the people carry. He even qualifies the seed theory as possibly his imagination. The report is urgent without becoming an omniscient enemy plan.

The company follows a blood-painted warning into the caverns and eventually brings people and a seed back. Aerrow’s place in that sequence is the scout who makes the need harder to ignore. A later death, departure or complete personal recovery is not established by the selected scenes. Read the captive rescue →

    Learning to use another hunter’s strengths

    Aerrow follows Aravil’s stealth, helps search for useful materials and urges the party to leave exposed battle sites.

    Known at this stage
    The group is unfamiliar with Babel’s ecology.
    Consequence
    Their different skills make a supply journey possible.
    Still unresolved

  2. 2026-01-06 · quest

    A healed body is not an untroubled mind

    After the aqualisk nearly breaks his body, Aerrow says he feels physically well but is still struggling with the memory.

    Known at this stage
    Arjahn’s healing has repaired the immediate injuries.
    Consequence
    Survival still requires time and attention after the fight.
    Still unresolved
    This is his immediate experience, not a diagnosis or a completed recovery.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4

  3. 2026-02-06 · quest

    Two deaths, one temporary Revivify

    Aerrow dies during the two-person hunt, returns through Arjahn’s Revivify and is killed again before the retreat.

    Known at this stage
    The escape is taking place under continued attack.
    Consequence
    Arjahn carries his body back; the final restoration happens in the later quest scene.
    Still unresolved
    Elenia’s later raising is shown without a named spell in the checked passage.
